title: Environmental Systems Engineering, B.S. (College of Earth and Mineral Sciences)
notes: University Park, Environmental Systems Engineering Option (ESE) -- the 'Fall 2024' plan specifically. IMPORTANT real finding from the raw archived 2024-25 bulletin: this catalog year's page carries a mid-year curriculum change banner -- 'Spring 2025 Curricular Update: The program description, entrance requirements, and program requirements detailed on this page are effective beginning Spring 2025... To view the requirements in effect for Fall 2024, please visit the 2024-25 Undergraduate Bulletin PDF.' The page's Program Requirements tab therefore already shows the NEW merged program (128 credits, single 'at All Campuses' plan, no more ESE/EHS option split -- structurally the ancestor of ENVSYS-2026.json). But its Suggested Academic Plan tab still separately preserves BOTH plans side by side: 'Effective Spring 2025' (the new merged one) and 'Fall 2024' (the old ESE/EHS-option-split one, 131-132 credits) -- and diffing the raw HTML shows the 'Fall 2024' table is byte-for-byte identical to the 2023-24 archived bulletin's own suggested plan (same GEOG 30N, PNG 411, MNG 401, MATH 220/231, and the 3-way 'EME 210, CMPSC 201, or CMPSC 203' slot). Since this file models a Fall-2024-entering student (self-verification simulates start_year=2024, today=2024-07-01, i.e. a Fall entrant -- NOT a Spring-2025 entrant), the correct real requirements for that student are the 'Fall 2024' plan, not the page's own currently-displayed Program Requirements tab (which is the post-update Spring-2025-forward plan and would misrepresent what a Fall 2024 entrant actually needed). This file is therefore built identically to ENVSYS-2023.json's ESE-option plan (same course list, same credits, same options) -- see that file's notes for the full rationale on: modeling ESE (not EHS) at University Park; GEOG 30N; PNG 411/MNG 401; the 3-way EME 210/CMPSC 201/CMPSC 203 elective; ENVSE 404W credited as 4 (shared catalogs/envse_catalog.json, not year-specific, vs. the bulletin's printed 3); the two 'Additional course from approved list for option' picks modeled as generic slots (SOILS 401 has an unmet prereq not in this plan); and the MATH 3/4/21/22 remediation chain added in Semester 1 for CHEM 110's/EME 210's real MATH 22 prereq. A student entering ENVSYS at University Park for Spring 2025 onward (rather than Fall 2024) would instead follow the same merged structure as ENVSYS-2025.json; that distinction doesn't have its own catalog_year slot in this app's per-year filing scheme and is called out here rather than silently dropped.
